scope: PHP 5.6.40 and 5.4.45 non-PIE FPM: 5.x geometry for the PHP 8.5 G2 (stale BG(unserialize) dtor-slot write) and G6 (session decode slot -> zif_system) chains, plus transfer verdict. Offline binary + DWARF + source analysis; no service started, no live exploit.

build.result: FPM target rc=0 for both trees; full make rc=2 on an unrelated link target
notes: -DHAVE_POSIX_READDIR_R=1 is mandatory: configure misdetects glibc's 3-arg readdir_r as legacy HAVE_OLD_READDIR_R.
Both binaries are ELF64 ET_EXEC (non-PIE) x86-64 with DWARF debug info.
5.4.45 source is the .tar.gz; the .tar.xz URL served an HTML error page.

bg_unserialize.layout: struct { void *var_hash; unsigned int level; } (level is 4 bytes + 4 bytes padding)

g2.bound: cmpq $0x400,0x2000(%rax); je 0x53193a -> _emalloc(0x2010), used_slots=0, next=0, link as last_dtor. The check is equality, not a range: every K except exactly 1024 writes at B0 + 8*K, so K < 0 (before data) and K > 1024 (past data) are both accepted.
g2.addref_variant: var_push_dtor: addl $1,0x10(%rax) on *rval (refcount at zval+0x10), then the same 8-byte store
g2.source_shape: ALLOC_INIT_ZVAL(current); php_var_unserialize(&current, ...); ... var_push_dtor_no_addref(&var_hash, &current) after the value (session.c php_binary decode). current is a separately allocated heap zval; the slot receives its address, not the zval contents.
g2.blocker: The slot receives an 8-byte pointer to a separately allocated zval. The 8.x G2 wrote the parsed typed 16-byte zval itself into the slot (var_tmp_var returns the slot). The value written by the 5.x G2 is therefore always a heap pointer, never an arbitrary 64-bit value such as zif_system.

php_exec_ex.failure_body: 0x4f1908 movq $0x0,(%rbx); 0x4f190f movb $0x3,0x14(%rbx)  -> RETURN_FALSE writes to address vallen

g6.parse_rejection: zend_parse_va_args (Zend/zend_API.c:729) checks num_args < min_num_args || num_args > max_num_args (5.6 :811; 5.4 :782). num_args = ht = low32(val), which for any realistic session buffer address is far outside 1..2. Even if it passed, the args are read from zend_vm_stack_top()-1 (5.6 :827) and the outer C frame has no matching argument zvals.
g6.verdict: No command execution. zend_parse_parameters fails, then RETURN_FALSE writes to address vallen (the session data length) and SIGSEGVs before exec. zif_passthru (mode 3) takes the same path.

request_order.plant: unserialize() with a value that triggers the user error handler -> E_USER_ERROR -> zend_bailout inside php_var_unserialize. PHP_VAR_UNSERIALIZE_DESTROY is not reached, so BG(unserialize).var_hash=P and BG(unserialize).level=1 survive the request.
request_order.next_request: php_hash_environment() runs before zend_activate_modules(); the rfc1867 session decode inside php_hash_environment calls PHP_VAR_UNSERIALIZE_INIT, sees level != 0, reuses P, and increments level to 2.

rinit_memset.5.6.40: PHP_RINIT_FUNCTION(basic) starts at ext/standard/basic_functions.c:3714; memset(&BG(unserialize),0,...) at :3720

rfc1867_update.5.6.40: php_session_rfc1867_update: php_session_initialize at ext/session/session.c:2645; php_session_flush at :2651. Each callback update re-initializes, so a second same-request decode occurs, still pre-RINIT.

request_order.conclusion: The stale-P primitive exists in 5.x and is consumed before RINIT, exactly like 8.x. The RINIT memset is not a blocker; it makes each plant single-shot (one pre-RINIT window).

slot_layout.8.5: var_dtor_entries { zend_long used_slots; void *next; zval data[255]; } -> data at +0x10, 16-byte typed zvals; slot = B0 + 0x10 + 16*K
slot_layout.5.x: var_entries { zval *data[1024]; long used_slots; void *next; } -> data at +0, 8-byte pointers; slot = B0 + 8*K

value_semantics.8.5: php_binary decode: current = var_tmp_var(&var_hash) returns &B0->data[used_slots]; php_var_unserialize(current, ...) writes the parsed typed zval directly into the slot. An IS_LONG with an arbitrary 64-bit value (e.g. libc system) lands in the slot.
value_semantics.5.x: php_binary decode: ALLOC_INIT_ZVAL(current); php_var_unserialize(&current, ...); var_push_dtor_no_addref(&var_hash, &current). The parsed typed zval lives in a separate heap allocation; the slot receives current (an 8-byte zval*).

comparison_8x.consequence: The 8.x G2 write value (arbitrary typed zval / arbitrary 64-bit value) does not exist in 5.x. The 5.x G2 is a heap-pointer write only.

verdict.g2: NO for the 8.x G2 shape (value transfer). The address arithmetic transfers with changed constants: A = B0 + 8*K, data[0] at B0, and an equality check that only special-cases K == 1024 (K < 0 and K > 1024 are accepted). But the slot store is an 8-byte zval* to a separately allocated zval, never an arbitrary 64-bit value. The 8.x ability to write IS_LONG = zif_system into the slot has no 5.x analogue.
verdict.g6: NO. 5.x decode => zif_system maps ht=(int)val, return_value=(zval*)vallen. zend_parse_parameters sees num_args = low32(session buffer address), fails the 1..2 check, and RETURN_FALSE writes 8 bytes to address vallen (the session data length) -> SIGSEGV before any exec. zif_passthru (mode 3) takes the same path. There is no execute_data parameter and no attacker-controlled VM frame; argument zvals come from the real VM stack.
verdict.stale_chain: YES as a primitive, not a blocker: pre-RINIT rfc1867 decode consumes the stale BG(unserialize) level=1/P exactly as in 8.x; single-shot per plant.
verdict.overall: The 5.x chain cannot reuse the 8.x G2 value write or the 8.x G6 decode-call shape. A 5.x-specific chain would need a different primitive (e.g. dereferencing the stored heap zval pointer), which is outside both shapes.
